checklist.step: Pull the prior-year figures the business-threshold test runs on
actions: In the general ledger run the statutory revenue report for the prior calendar year at consolidated group level and note gross annual revenues before any deduction.
Ask the Chief Financial Officer's reporting team to confirm which legal entities roll into the CCPA control group so affiliates sharing the Meridian brand are counted.
Split out any revenue line attributable to advertising, lead sales or data monetisation and give the total to the Privacy Office for the 50%-of-revenue limb.
Send the signed revenue extract to the Privacy Officer with the extraction date and the report id.
checklist.done: prior-year gross revenue, the control-group entity list and the data-monetisation revenue line are delivered in writing to the Privacy Office.

checklist.step: Count California consumers and households whose PI was bought, sold or shared
actions: Query the customer, prospect and web-analytics marts for distinct California residents and households with PI processed in the prior calendar year, keying on state of residence and IP geolocation.
Separately count records that were bought, sold or shared — third-party lead purchases, co-marketing feeds and advertising-pixel audiences handed to ad platforms.
Deduplicate against the MDM golden record so one household is not counted once per policy or quote.
Save the counting SQL, run date and row counts to the shared privacy workspace so the number is reproducible.
checklist.done: a reproducible count of California consumers/households, with a separate bought-sold-shared subtotal, is filed with the query that produced it.

checklist.step: Run and write the 1798.140(d) 'business' threshold analysis
actions: Open the CPPA website and read the current CPI-adjusted gross-revenue threshold for the applicable year (statutory base 25,000,000 USD as adjusted).

Test each limb in turn on the memo: (a) gross revenue against the adjusted threshold, (b) 100,000 or more California consumers or households bought, sold or shared, (c) 50% or more of annual revenue from selling or sharing PI.
Record for each limb the tested value, the source document and PASS/FAIL, and state the overall conclusion on whether Meridian is a 'business'.
Add the GLBA analysis under 1798.145(e): state that GLBA-regulated non-public personal information is exempt but that the entity-level obligations still bite on non-GLBA data.
Sign and date the memo and file it as CCPA-Threshold-Analysis-<year> in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed, dated threshold memo states a tested value, a source and a pass/fail for each of the three limbs plus the GLBA carve-out conclusion.

checklist.step: Refresh the register of California collection points
actions: Walk each channel with its owner — Digital Channel Manager for web and app, Marketing Manager for landing pages, Contact Center Ops Manager for IVR and agent screens, HR Business Partner for applicant and employee forms.
Add a register row per collection point: URL or screen id, owning team, PI categories captured, purpose, whether sensitive PI is captured, and whether the data flows to an ad platform.
Cross-check against the tag manager inventory and the API gateway route list so background collection (pixels, SDKs, chat widgets) is registered, not just visible forms.
Retire rows for collection points decommissioned in the year, keeping the retirement date.
checklist.done: the register has one row per live California collection point with PI categories, purpose and downstream ad-platform flag, reconciled to the tag inventory.

checklist.step: Map each collection point's fields to the statutory PI categories
actions: For each register row list the captured fields and map them to the 1798.140(v) categories (identifiers, commercial information, internet activity, geolocation, inferences, and so on).
Flag sensitive PI under 1798.140(ae) — driver's licence number, precise geolocation, health data, racial or ethnic origin — because it drives the Limit-Use link.
Set a retention period per category with the Records Manager and record it, since 11 CCR 7012 requires the retention period or the criteria in the notice.
Publish the mapping back onto each register row so the notice writer works from data, not memory.
checklist.done: every collection point carries a field-to-category map, a sensitive-PI flag and a stated retention period.

checklist.step: Draft the notice-at-collection text for each collection point
actions: For each register row draft notice text containing: the categories of PI collected, the purpose of each category, the retention period or criteria, whether the category is sold or shared, and a link to the full privacy policy.
Where the collection point sells or shares PI, add the Notice of Right to Opt Out and the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link per 11 CCR 7013.
Where sensitive PI is captured for a non-exempt purpose, add the 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' link per 1798.121.
Keep the wording at a plain-language reading level and produce the Spanish version where the collection point is offered in Spanish.
Hand the drafts to Privacy Counsel with the register row and the field map attached.
checklist.done: each collection point has draft notice text covering categories, purposes, retention, sale/share status and the required links, in every language the point is offered in.

checklist.step: Get Privacy Counsel to clear the notice text and the placement
actions: Read each draft against 11 CCR 7012 and confirm the notice appears at or before the moment of collection, not after submission.
Reject any design that hides the notice behind a scroll, a hover or a post-submit confirmation page.
Confirm the sale/share statement matches what the ad-platform flag on the register row actually says, and challenge any mismatch with the Digital Marketing Specialist.
Stamp each approved version with a version number, approval date and counsel name, and return the rejected ones with the specific defect.
checklist.done: every notice version is either counsel-approved with a version stamp or returned with a named defect and a rework date.

checklist.step: Deploy the notice on the web and mobile collection points
actions: Place the approved notice text above the first PI field on each quote, application and account form, and on the app onboarding screen before the first field renders.
Add the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' and 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' links to the site footer on every California-served page.
Confirm the notice renders on mobile viewport and with a screen reader, and that the privacy-policy link resolves to the current version.
Take a dated full-page capture of every deployed surface and send it to the Records Manager as evidence.
checklist.done: the approved notice renders at or above the first PI field on every web and app collection point, with footer links live and dated captures filed.

checklist.step: Deploy the oral notice in the contact centre and on agent intake screens
actions: Load the approved oral notice into the IVR prompt set so it plays before the first prompt that captures PI, and into the agent desktop script above the data-capture panel.
Add the alternative-format offer required by 11 CCR 7012(g) for telephone collection — direct the caller to the URL where the written notice sits.
Update the agent knowledge article with the exact wording and add it to the call-quality scorecard as a scored behaviour.
Export the prompt configuration and the script version as dated evidence.
checklist.done: the IVR plays the notice before the first PI capture, the agent script shows it above the capture panel, and both are scored in call QA.

checklist.step: Refresh the online privacy policy on its 12-month cycle
actions: Rebuild the privacy policy from the register: categories collected, sources, business and commercial purposes, third parties disclosed to, retention, sale/share disclosure and the consumer rights list with how to exercise each.
State the two request channels (toll-free number and web form) and the verification process, and add the metrics disclosure block if the 10,000,000-consumer threshold in 11 CCR 7102 is met.
Set the last-updated date on the page to the publication date and archive the superseded version with its own effective-date range.
Publish, then confirm the footer link on every California-served page and the app resolve to the new version.
checklist.done: a rebuilt privacy policy is live with a current last-updated date, the prior version archived with its date range, and every footer link resolving to it.

checklist.step: Deliver the notice at collection to employees and job applicants
actions: Attach the HR-specific notice at collection to the job-application form so it renders before the applicant enters any field, and to the new-hire onboarding task list as a required acknowledgement.
Cover the HR-specific categories: identifiers, background-check results, benefits and dependant data, and any sensitive PI such as immigration status.
Record the acknowledgement date per applicant and per employee in the HRIS so it can be produced per person.
Send the annual re-issue to the existing California workforce and reconcile the acknowledgement list to active headcount.
checklist.done: every California applicant sees the notice before entering data and every California employee has a dated acknowledgement on file.

checklist.step: Wire the notice check into the release and campaign change gates
actions: Add a mandatory 'new or changed California data capture?' question to the release checklist and to the campaign brief template.
Where the answer is yes, block launch until the Privacy Office adds the register row and the approved notice is attached to the landing page template.
Audit the live landing-page templates monthly for forms published without the notice block and pull any that fail.
Report gate breaches to the Privacy Officer with the campaign id and the launch date.
checklist.done: no release or campaign that adds a California capture field can launch without a register row and an attached approved notice.

checklist.step: Capture and file dated evidence of every notice surface
actions: Collect the full-page captures, IVR prompt exports, HRIS acknowledgement extracts and privacy-policy archives into a single dated evidence bundle per quarter.
Index each artefact by collection point, notice version number, effective-from and effective-to date.
Apply the 7-year retention label so the evidence outlives the collection point it documents.
Confirm the index returns a result when searched by URL, by notice version and by date.
checklist.done: a quarterly evidence bundle exists, indexed by collection point and notice version, under a 7-year retention label.

checklist.step: Log and drive out notice exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every collection point found live without a conforming notice, recording the first-collection date, the days exposed and the count of records collected in that window.
Assign a root cause (register row never created, release bypassed the gate, notice text stale after a field change, vendor tag added outside change control) and an owner.
Set the remediation date at no later than 15 business days from detection and track it to closure.
Refer any exposure involving sensitive PI or ad-platform sharing to Privacy Counsel for a re-notice decision.
checklist.done: every notice gap has an issue with days exposed, records affected, root cause, owner and a remediation date inside 15 business days.

checklist.step: Attest the annual notice and threshold position
actions: Review the signed threshold memo, the collection-point register, the notice version history and the open exception list in one sitting.

Sign the annual attestation that every live California collection point carried a conforming notice at or before collection and the privacy policy was refreshed inside 12 months, listing any exception by name.
Table the attestation and the exception list at the Privacy Governance Committee and record the minute reference.
File the signed attestation with the year's evidence bundle.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation naming every exception exists, tabled at the Privacy Governance Committee with a minute reference.

testing.step: Build the population of California collection points that were live in the year
actions: Export the collection-point register with effective-from and effective-to dates for the test year.
Independently crawl meridian.com and the mobile app for forms containing PI fields, and pull the tag manager container export and the API gateway route list for background collectors.
Add the Marketo landing-page inventory and the HRIS application form list so marketing and HR capture points are in the same population.
Merge and deduplicate into one population file with a source column showing where each row was discovered.
testing.done: a single deduplicated population of California collection points exists with the discovery source recorded for each row.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the register and prove the register is complete
actions: Match each crawled or tag-derived collection point to a register row on URL or screen id.
List every collection point found in the crawl but absent from the register — these are completeness failures, not documentation gaps.
List register rows with no live surface and confirm each has a retirement date.
Ask the Data Privacy Steward to explain each unmatched row in writing and attach the reply.
testing.done: every discovered collection point is either matched to a register row or listed as a completeness exception with a written explanation.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of collection points capturing sensitive PI and 100% of those flagged as feeding an advertising platform.
Take 25 further rows at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, with a floor of 40 rows in total.
Record population size, seed, selection date and the strata definitions in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Include every privacy-policy version published in the year as a separate 100% stratum.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers all sensitive-PI and ad-sharing collection points.

testing.step: Re-perform the notice-at-collection test on each sampled surface
actions: Open each sampled form in a clean browser session with a California IP and record whether the notice is visible before the first PI field, without scrolling past a capture field.
For IVR rows, place a test call and time-stamp whether the notice plays before the first PI prompt.
Score placement independently first, then compare to the register's claimed placement; a notice appearing only after submit is a fail.
Capture a dated screenshot or call recording reference into the workpaper for every sampled row.
testing.done: each sampled surface has an independent placement verdict backed by a dated capture or call recording.

testing.step: Test the notice content against the statutory content list
actions: For each sampled notice tick off: PI categories, purpose per category, retention period or criteria, sale/share statement, privacy-policy link, and the opt-out and Limit-Use links where required.
Compare the listed categories to the actual form fields and to the field-to-category map — an unlisted field is a content failure.
Confirm the sale/share statement agrees with the ad-platform tags actually firing on the page, checked in the browser network panel.
Log each missing element by element name rather than as a general 'notice deficient' finding.
testing.done: every sampled notice has an element-by-element content score and any missing element is named.

testing.step: Trace the privacy-policy version history and the 12-month refresh
actions: Pull every archived privacy-policy version with its effective-from and effective-to date.
Compute the gap between consecutive last-updated dates and flag any interval exceeding 12 months.
Check each version carries a visible last-updated date on the page as published, using the archived capture, not a re-rendered copy.
Confirm the version live on any given sampled collection date is the one the notice link resolved to.
testing.done: the version chain is unbroken, no refresh interval exceeds 12 months, and each version shows its own last-updated date.

testing.step: Recompute the business-threshold maths independently
actions: Re-pull prior-year gross revenue from the general ledger yourself and compare to the figure used in the threshold memo.
Re-run the California consumer/household count from the warehouse using the steward's saved SQL and compare row counts.
Re-read the CPI-adjusted revenue threshold published by the CPPA for the relevant year and confirm the memo used that figure, not the unadjusted 25,000,000 USD base.
Recompute the 50%-of-revenue limb from the data-monetisation revenue line and confirm the stated conclusion follows from the three limbs.
testing.done: each threshold limb is independently recomputed and agrees with the memo, or the difference is quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the opt-out and Limit-Use links function from the sampled pages
actions: Click the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link from each sampled page and confirm it lands on a working request mechanism, not a general contact page.
Do the same for 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' on every sensitive-PI collection point.
Send a Global Privacy Control signal from the browser and confirm the page treats it as an opt-out request per 11 CCR 7025.
Record the destination URL, the response and the test timestamp for each link.
testing.done: every required link resolves to a working request mechanism and the GPC signal is honoured, with timestamps recorded.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the collection point, the defect type (placement, content, register completeness, policy staleness, threshold maths) and the exposure window.
Assign a root cause and a named owner from the channel that owns the surface, not from the Privacy Office by default.
Set remediation dates and mark any exception involving sensitive PI or ad-platform sharing for Privacy Counsel review of consumer re-notice.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a defect type, exposure window, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the notice-coverage rate and the content-completeness rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance placement threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or deployed no sampled notice, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open exceptions to the Privacy Governance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion, the coverage rate and the committee reporting date, filed in the evidence repository.

Code 1798.105 (deletion), 1798.120/.135 (opt-out of sale and sharing) and the GLBA carve-out at 1798.145(e), read with CPPA regulations 11 CCR 7020-7022 (request handling), 7021 (timelines) and 7026 (opt-out); the GLBA scoping line is re-read whenever a new non-insurance data source is onboarded

In-scope processes.value: Intake, verification, fulfilment and closure of know/access, delete, correct, opt-out of sale-or-share and limit-sensitive-PI requests from California residents — restricted to non-GLBA populations: web visitors, unconverted prospects, marketing contacts, employees, job applicants and B2B contacts

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Privacy Officer with Privacy Counsel concurrence; reviewed twice yearly and re-opened whenever a new non-GLBA data source (a marketing platform, an HR system, a chat widget) joins the fan-out list

checklist.step: Keep both statutory intake channels live and instrumented
actions: Confirm the toll-free privacy line answers, routes to the privacy queue and logs an interaction id on every call, and test it from an outside line at the start of each month.
Confirm the web privacy request form on meridian.com submits, returns a reference number and creates a case, testing an end-to-end submission monthly.
Publish both channels in the privacy policy and in the notice at collection, with the number and the URL stated verbatim.
Set an alert so a channel outage longer than one business hour raises a P2 incident to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: both the toll-free line and the web form are proven working by a dated monthly end-to-end test, with outages alerting the Privacy Officer.

checklist.step: Log every incoming request into the case tool the day it arrives
actions: Sweep the four intake surfaces daily — web form queue, telephony privacy queue, privacy@ inbox and postal scans — and create a case for each request.
Stamp the receipt date as the calendar date the request first arrived at any channel, not the date it reached Privacy Ops.
Record request type (know/access, delete, correct, opt-out of sale-or-share, limit sensitive PI), channel, claimed identity and any authorised-agent indication.
Start the 45-calendar-day clock and the 10-business-day confirmation clock on the case from that receipt date.
checklist.done: every request has a case with the true first-touch receipt date and both SLA clocks running.

checklist.step: Send the confirmation of receipt inside 10 business days
actions: Issue the templated acknowledgement within 10 business days of receipt, stating how the request will be processed and the expected response date.
Send it by the same medium the consumer used unless they asked otherwise, and attach the sent copy to the case.
Where the consumer used the toll-free line and left no written address, record the call-back confirmation and the agent id.
Escalate to the Data Privacy Steward any case still unconfirmed on business day 8.
checklist.done: a dated confirmation of receipt is attached to every case within 10 business days, or the case is escalated before day 10.

checklist.step: Verify the requester to the tier the request demands
actions: Apply the verification tier: two data points for a categories-only request, three for specific pieces of PI, plus a signed declaration under penalty of perjury for specific pieces per 11 CCR 7062.
Match the offered data points against the customer master and the marketing contact record — never against data the requester supplied in the same request.
For authorised agents, obtain the written permission, verify the agent, and verify the consumer directly unless a power of attorney is produced.
Record the verification outcome, the data points matched and the decision date on the case; where verification fails, send the denial explaining what was insufficient.
checklist.done: every case carries a recorded verification tier, the matched data points and a dated verify/deny decision.

checklist.step: Decide the GLBA versus non-GLBA scope of the request
actions: Determine which populations the requester sits in: policyholder or claimant (GLBA non-public personal information, exempt under 1798.145(e)) versus web visitor, unconverted prospect, marketing contact, employee, applicant or B2B contact.
Where the requester spans both, scope the request to the non-GLBA records only and say so plainly in the response rather than refusing outright.
Cite the exemption limb relied on and the population evidence on the case, so the call can be re-read later.
Refer any novel population — a new data broker feed, an embedded-insurance partner list — to the register maintenance step before answering.
checklist.done: each case records which populations are in scope, which are GLBA-exempt, and the citation behind the split.

checklist.step: Maintain the register of non-GLBA PI categories that keeps requests in scope
actions: Hold one register row per non-GLBA population — web visitors, prospects, marketing contacts, employees, job applicants, B2B contacts — with its PI categories, source systems, processing purposes and retention.
Name for each row the systems that must be searched on a request: the CRM, the marketing automation platform, the web analytics store, the HRIS, the recruiting system and the chat transcript store.
Re-run a quarterly reconciliation against the data catalog so a newly onboarded source cannot sit outside the register.
Publish the register to the DSAR runbook so fulfilment works from it rather than from tribal knowledge.
checklist.done: the register lists every non-GLBA population with its PI categories and the exact systems to search, reconciled quarterly to the data catalog.

checklist.step: Fan the verified request out to every system on the register
actions: Run the standard search identifiers — email, phone, cookie or device id, employee id — against each system named on the register rows in scope.
Record per system: searched by whom, on what date, with what identifier, and the record count returned, including nil returns.
Task system owners who cannot be searched centrally with a written return by a stated date at least 10 calendar days before the response deadline.
Attach every system return to the case so the response can be rebuilt from evidence.
checklist.done: every in-scope system has a dated, identified search return attached to the case, nil returns included.

checklist.step: Assemble the access or correction response package
actions: For an access request, build the disclosure covering the 12-month lookback (or longer where the consumer asks and the data supports it): categories collected, sources, purposes, third parties disclosed to and the specific pieces where verified to that tier.

Redact other individuals' PI and withhold the categories 11 CCR 7024(d) prohibits disclosing — Social Security number, driver's licence, financial account number, precise geolocation, account passwords and security answers.
For a correction request, apply the correction at the system of record first, then push it through the downstream systems and note each one.
Deliver in a portable, readily usable format through a secure channel and record the delivery method and date.
checklist.done: the response package is complete, correctly redacted, delivered securely and its delivery date is recorded on the case.

checklist.step: Execute deletion requests across the register systems
actions: Choose the method per system — permanent erasure, de-identification or aggregation — and record which was used and why.

Name every retention exception relied on under 1798.105(d) (completing the transaction, security incident detection, legal obligation, internal uses reasonably aligned with expectations) with the record set it covers.
Suppress rather than re-collect: add the identifier to the marketing suppression list so the next campaign import cannot resurrect the record.
Confirm and record the deletion count per system and attach the confirmations to the case.
checklist.done: each deletion has a per-system method, a counted confirmation, a named exception for anything retained and a suppression entry.

checklist.step: Action opt-out of sale or sharing within 15 business days
actions: Set the opt-out flag on the consumer record and push it to every advertising and analytics destination on the sharing list within 15 business days of receipt.
Send the downstream notification to third parties that received the PI in the 90 days before the request, as 11 CCR 7026(f)(2) requires, and log the acknowledgements.
Honour Global Privacy Control signals as valid opt-outs without asking the consumer to confirm.
Record the effective date of each destination suppression on the case.
checklist.done: the opt-out is live at every sharing destination within 15 business days, with 90-day downstream notifications logged.

checklist.step: Take the 45-day extension deliberately, in writing, inside the first window
actions: Review every case still open at day 30 and decide whether an extension is genuinely needed, recording the reason (volume, complexity, number of systems).
Where extending, send the consumer written notice inside the original 45 calendar days stating the reason and the new response date, capped at a further 45 days.
Reset the case SLA to the extended date and mark the case as extended so it lands in the quarterly deep-dive.
Refuse extensions raised after day 45 and treat those cases as late, not extended.
checklist.done: every extended case has a written extension notice sent inside the first 45 days with a reason and a capped new date.

checklist.step: Close the case with the response, the reasoning and the appeal route
actions: Send the substantive response by day 45 (or the notified extended date) covering what was found, what was done and what was withheld.
For any denial or partial denial state the basis — verification failure, GLBA exemption, a 1798.105(d) retention exception — and the citation.
Give the consumer the route to challenge: the privacy team contact and the CPPA complaint path.
Stamp the response date on the case and attach the sent copy and any delivery receipt.
checklist.done: each case closes with a dated, delivered response, a cited basis for anything withheld and the challenge route stated.

checklist.step: Report the DSAR metrics and keep the SLA dashboard honest
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard of requests received, complied with in whole or part, denied, and the median days to respond, split by request type as 11 CCR 7102 frames it.
Reconcile the dashboard count to the case-tool extract and the telephony privacy-queue count before publishing.
Feed the annual figures into the privacy-policy metrics disclosure where the 10,000,000-consumer threshold applies.
Send the dashboard to the Privacy Officer and the Privacy Governance Committee each month.
checklist.done: a reconciled monthly metrics dashboard is published with counts by request type and median response days.

checklist.step: Log SLA breaches and drive the root cause out
actions: Raise an issue for every case answered after day 45 without a valid extension notice and every opt-out effected after 15 business days.
Record the day count, the request type, the stage that consumed the time and a root cause (intake lag, verification stall, a system owner missing the internal return date).
Assign the owner to the function that caused the delay and set a remediation date.
Track repeat root causes across months and raise a control change where the same cause appears twice.
checklist.done: every late case and late opt-out has an issue with a day count, a stage-level root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

checklist.step: Retain the DSAR log and case evidence for the statutory period
actions: Archive each closed case with its intake record, verification evidence, scoping decision, system search returns, response letter and delivery proof.
Apply the 24-month minimum retention required by 11 CCR 7101 and the 7-year internal label, whichever is longer.
Confirm the archive is searchable by consumer reference, request type, receipt date and response date.
Prove restoration once a quarter by retrieving three closed cases at random and checking every artefact opens.
checklist.done: closed cases are archived complete, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by a quarterly restoration test.

testing.step: Build the population of California rights requests received in the period
actions: Extract every DSAR case with receipt date inside the period, with channel, request type, confirmation date, verification outcome, extension flag and response date.
Pull independent channel records: the telephony privacy-queue interaction log, the web form submission log, the privacy inbox message list and the postal scan register.
Merge the channel records against the case extract to find requests that never became cases.
Freeze the population file with a row count and an extraction timestamp before any sampling.
testing.done: a frozen population exists combining case records and raw channel logs, with an extraction timestamp.

testing.step: Reconcile the case tool to the raw intake channels
actions: Match each web submission, privacy-queue call and privacy inbox message to a case on reference number, phone number or email.
List unmatched intake events and require Privacy Ops to explain each in writing — an unlogged request is an intake control failure.
Compare the case receipt date to the raw channel timestamp and flag any case whose receipt date was set later than first touch.
Quantify the total unlogged and back-dated count in the workpaper.
testing.done: every raw intake event is matched to a case or explained, and back-dated receipt dates are quantified.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of denied requests, 100% of extended requests and 100% of opt-out requests.
Take 30 further cases at random across the remaining request types using a recorded seed.
Record population size, strata sizes, seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add any case flagged in the prior month's exceptions as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all denials, extensions and opt-outs, plus a seeded random tail, and is reproducible.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory day count from the raw timestamps
actions: Recompute confirmation days as business days from raw channel timestamp to confirmation send, and fail anything above 10.
Recompute response days as calendar days from raw receipt to response delivery, and fail anything above 45 without a valid extension.
For extended cases, check the extension notice date falls inside the first 45 days and that the extended date is no more than 45 further days.
For opt-outs, recompute business days from receipt to the destination suppression effective date and fail anything above 15.
testing.done: every sampled case has independently recomputed day counts against the 10, 45, 45 and 15-day tests.

testing.step: Re-perform the identity verification decision
actions: Read the verification evidence on each sampled case and decide the tier yourself before reading the recorded outcome.
Check specific-pieces requests carry three matched data points plus the signed declaration under penalty of perjury.
Confirm the matching used pre-existing record data, not data the requester supplied in the same message.
Flag any case fulfilled with a weaker verification than the request type demands as an over-disclosure exception, and any denial on thin grounds as an under-service exception.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent verification verdict and any over-disclosure or under-service is flagged.

testing.step: Trace the fulfilment back to the register of non-GLBA systems
actions: Pull the register rows applicable to each sampled requester's populations and list the systems that should have been searched.
Compare that list to the search returns actually attached to the case and name every system with no return.
Open two returns per case and confirm the identifier searched matches the requester's identifiers.
Treat a missing system return as an incomplete response, not a filing gap.
testing.done: each sampled case shows a search return for every register system in scope, or the missing system is named as an exception.

testing.step: Test the GLBA scoping calls independently
actions: For each sampled case read the recorded population evidence and re-decide whether the data was GLBA non-public personal information or non-GLBA.
Challenge any blanket GLBA refusal where the requester also existed as a web visitor, marketing contact or job applicant.
Confirm the response letter told the consumer which categories were out of scope and why, rather than refusing without explanation.
Record agreement or disagreement per case with the citation you relied on.
testing.done: every sampled scoping call is independently re-decided and any blanket refusal is challenged in writing.

testing.step: Verify the deletion and opt-out actually took effect downstream
actions: For sampled deletions, search the CRM, marketing platform and warehouse for the identifiers 30 days after closure and confirm no live record returned outside a named retention exception.
Confirm the identifier sits on the marketing suppression list so a later import cannot reintroduce it.
For sampled opt-outs, confirm the suppression flag reached each advertising destination and that the 90-day downstream notification acknowledgements are on file.
Record any resurrection with the system, the date it reappeared and the import that caused it.
testing.done: no sampled deleted or opted-out identifier is live downstream without a named exception, and any resurrection is traced to its import.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the case reference, the failed test (10-day, 45-day, 15-day, verification, completeness, downstream effect) and the day count or record count.
Assign a stage-level root cause and a named owner in the function that consumed the time.
Set a remediation date and, for any late statutory response, require Privacy Counsel to decide whether the consumer needs a corrective communication.
Carry open exceptions into the next monthly run as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a failed-test label, a measured overrun, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign independently and report the SLA position
actions: Compute the on-time rate for each of the 10-business-day, 45-calendar-day and 15-business-day tests and compare to the 100% target.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled no sampled case, sign the workpaper.
Report the rates, breach count and open exceptions to the Privacy Governance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three on-time rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Civ. Code 1798.100 (collection, purpose limitation and retention disclosure), 1798.110 (right to know categories and specific pieces) and 1798.115 (disclosure and sale/share categories), read with 1798.130 response timing and 11 CCR 7021 (45 days from receipt, one 45-day extension) and 7002 (purposes reasonably necessary and proportionate)

In-scope systems.value: Processing register and lineage held in the data catalog over the CRM, marketing platform, policy administration, HRIS, warehouse and web analytics stores; the deadline ledger is a linked register with per-request day counts

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register attestation refreshed quarterly and fully re-baselined annually; every verifiable access request tracked from receipt date with a hard 45-calendar-day response, a documented extension of up to a further 45 days notified inside the first window, and the 10-business-day confirmation logged alongside

Deadline reminders configured.value: Ledger alerts at day 30 (extension decision), day 40 (response draft due) and day 44 (breach imminent) routed to the record owner and the Privacy Officer, plus quarterly register-attestation tasks issued to each system owner 30 days before the attestation date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Versioned register snapshots with attestation signatures, lineage exports and the deadline ledger with per-request day counts, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A PI store found outside the register, a processing purpose with no recorded business purpose, or an access request breaching 45 days without a notified extension is logged with the store or request reference, the exposure and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The DPO signs each quarterly register attestation and every remediation closing an unregistered PI store or a breached 45-day response

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All registered PI stores and processing purposes as at the test date, reconciled to the system inventory, plus every verifiable access request with a receipt date in the test quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unregistered PI stores; zero register rows lacking purpose, business purpose, retention or disclosure mapping; zero access responses beyond 45 calendar days without an extension notice inside the first window; any single breach reports to the Data Governance Council and the DPO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so completeness testing of the register runs quarterly against the system inventory and the day-count recomputation runs monthly over that month's closed access requests

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own, maintain or attest any register row or handle any tested access request

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly register completeness workpaper and monthly day-count workpaper (population, reconciliation, sample, re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under CCPA / Processing Register / <year>-Q<n>

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Counsel owns the CPPA response; the Data Governance Lead supplies the register extract and the DPO confirms it matches the attested version before release

checklist.step: Rebuild the inventory of systems that hold California personal information
actions: Export every application from the configuration management database with a data-classification tag of Confidential or Restricted and an owner.
Add the shadow surfaces the CMDB misses: SaaS marketing tools, chat widgets, survey platforms, analytics SDKs and file shares holding extracts.
Confirm with each application owner in writing whether the system holds California resident PI and which populations it covers.
Hand the confirmed list to the Data Governance Lead as the candidate register scope with an as-at date.
checklist.done: a dated, owner-confirmed inventory of every system holding California PI exists, including SaaS and shadow surfaces.

checklist.step: Profile each store down to field level and tag the PI categories
actions: Run the classification scanner across each in-scope schema and produce a column-level report of detected PI patterns (email, phone, SSN, licence number, geolocation, health markers).
Map each detected column to a 1798.140(v) category and flag sensitive PI under 1798.140(ae).
Review false positives with the system owner and record accepted classifications on the column.
Report unclassified columns holding free text so they are triaged rather than silently ignored.
checklist.done: every in-scope schema has column-level PI classification with sensitive-PI flags and no untriaged free-text column.

checklist.step: Record the collection purpose and the business purpose for each category
actions: For each PI category in each store, write the purpose of collection in plain terms and map it to a named business purpose from 1798.140(e) such as auditing, security, debugging, servicing accounts or quality assurance.
Apply the 11 CCR 7002 test — is the purpose reasonably necessary and proportionate to what a consumer would expect at that collection point — and record the reasoning, not just a yes.
Flag any secondary use that a consumer would not expect and route it to the assessment item before it continues.
Have the system owner countersign the purpose statement for their store.
checklist.done: every category-store pair carries a stated purpose, a named business purpose, a proportionality reasoning line and an owner countersignature.

checklist.step: Attach the retention period and the deletion trigger to each register row
actions: Map each register row to the corporate retention schedule and record the retention period or, where no fixed period applies, the criteria used to set it.
Where insurance regulation drives a longer hold, cite it so the CCPA disclosure can explain the longer period honestly.
Record the deletion trigger — policy termination plus n years, contact inactivity, applicant rejection plus n months — and the job or process that fires it.
Escalate any row with no retention basis to the DPO rather than defaulting to indefinite.
checklist.done: no register row lacks a retention period or stated criteria, a deletion trigger and the process that executes it.

checklist.step: Map the disclosure, sale and sharing recipients per category
actions: For each register row list every recipient: service providers, contractors, third parties, advertising platforms and affiliates, with the contract reference.
Classify each flow as a business-purpose disclosure, a sale, or a sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising, and record which limb of 1798.140 you relied on.
Confirm the flow list against the outbound integration inventory on the API gateway and the file-transfer job list so undocumented feeds surface.
Publish the recipient map into the register row so the right-to-know response can be built from it directly.
checklist.done: each register row shows named recipients, a sale/share/disclosure classification and a contract reference, reconciled to outbound integrations.

checklist.step: Record lineage from collection point through to every downstream store
actions: Capture the pipeline lineage from each collection point through the warehouse into every mart and extract that carries the PI category.
Record the transformation stage at which data is pseudonymised or aggregated, since that changes what must be disclosed.
Link each lineage node to the register row so a right-to-know search knows every stop the data made.
Refresh lineage on every pipeline release rather than on an annual cycle.
checklist.done: lineage from collection point to final store is captured per PI category and refreshed on pipeline release.

checklist.step: Publish the register and hold the quarterly owner attestation
actions: Issue each system owner their register rows 30 days before the attestation date with the fields they must confirm.
Require the owner to confirm or correct purposes, categories, retention and recipients, and to declare any new processing added in the quarter.
Chase non-responders at day 15 and day 25 and escalate day-30 non-response to the DPO.
Snapshot and version the attested register with the attestation date and the signing owner per row.
checklist.done: a versioned register snapshot exists with a dated per-row owner attestation and all non-responders escalated.

checklist.step: Open the deadline ledger entry the moment an access request is verified
actions: Create a ledger row per verifiable access request holding: consumer reference, receipt date, confirmation-sent date, verification date, target response date at receipt plus 45 calendar days.
Set the 12-month lookback window on the row, extending it where the consumer asks and the data supports a longer period.
List the register rows in scope for the request so fulfilment works from the register, not from search guesses.
Link the ledger row to the case so the day count and the fulfilment evidence stay together.
checklist.done: every verifiable access request has a ledger row with receipt date, computed 45-day target and the in-scope register rows named.

checklist.step: Assemble the right-to-know disclosure from the register, not from ad hoc queries
actions: Pull the categories collected, the sources, the business and commercial purposes and the recipient categories straight from the register rows named on the ledger row.
Run the specific-pieces extraction across the lineage nodes for those rows using the consumer's identifiers, recording the count returned per node.
Apply the 11 CCR 7024(d) withholding list and note each withheld element by name on the ledger row.
Attach the assembled disclosure to the ledger row with the extraction date.
checklist.done: the disclosure is built from named register rows and lineage nodes, with withheld elements named and the extraction dated.

checklist.step: Run the day-30 extension decision on every open ledger row
actions: Review every ledger row still open at day 30 against the fulfilment progress recorded per register row.
Where an extension is required, send written notice to the consumer inside the original 45 calendar days stating the reason and the new date, capped at 45 further days.
Update the ledger row with the extension date, the reason code and the notice evidence.
Where no extension is justified, escalate the blocking system owner in writing the same day.
checklist.done: every row open at day 30 has either a notified extension inside the first 45 days or a written escalation of the blocker.

checklist.step: Close the ledger row when the response is delivered and count the days
actions: Record the response delivery date and the delivery method on the ledger row.
Compute the elapsed calendar days from receipt to delivery and store the number on the row rather than a pass flag alone.
Mark any row over 45 days without a notified extension as BREACH and raise the exception the same day.
Attach the delivered response and the delivery receipt to the row before closing it.
checklist.done: every closed row carries a stored elapsed-day count, the delivered response and a BREACH marker where the 45 days ran out.

checklist.step: Publish the register-to-request reconciliation each month
actions: Report the count of open and closed ledger rows, the elapsed-day distribution, the extension rate and the breach count for the month.
Report register health alongside: rows attested, rows overdue for attestation, unregistered stores found and purposes flagged as disproportionate.
Reconcile the ledger count to the DSAR case count so a request cannot be fulfilled without a ledger row.
Circulate to the DPO, the Privacy Officer and the Data Governance Council.
checklist.done: a monthly report ties ledger day counts and register health together and reconciles to the DSAR case count.

checklist.step: Log register and timing exceptions with a disposition
actions: Raise an issue for every unregistered PI store, every register row missing purpose, retention or recipients, and every breached 45-day response.
Record the exposure — records held, consumers affected, days over deadline — and the root cause.
Assign the owner to the system owner or the fulfilment function that caused it, with a remediation date inside 30 days.
Suspend new processing on any store that remains unregistered past its remediation date until the register row is complete.
checklist.done: every register gap and timing breach has an issue with quantified exposure, root cause, owner and a 30-day remediation date.

checklist.step: Feed the register into the notice and vendor controls so it is actually used
actions: Regenerate the privacy-policy category, purpose, retention and recipient sections from the attested register rather than editing prose by hand.
Send the recipient map to Procurement so every named recipient can be tied back to a contract with the required CCPA clauses.
Send the sensitive-PI rows to the assessment owner so high-risk processing is picked up.
Record in the register which downstream artefact consumed each row and when.
checklist.done: the privacy policy, the vendor contract list and the assessment backlog are all regenerated from the attested register with dates recorded.

checklist.step: Version, retain and prove retrievability of register snapshots and the ledger
actions: File each quarterly register snapshot with its attestation signatures and each monthly ledger extract with the day counts.
Apply the 7-year retention label and record the as-at date on every artefact.
Confirm the archive answers a query by PI category, by system and by consumer reference.
Restore three artefacts at random each quarter and confirm they open with signatures intact.
checklist.done: register snapshots and ledger extracts are retained 7 years, indexed by category and system, and proven retrievable quarterly.

testing.step: Build the population of systems and processing purposes claimed to be registered
actions: Export the attested register as at the quarter end with every row, its owner, attestation date and completeness fields.
Independently pull the CMDB application list, the SaaS spend list from Procurement and the outbound integration list from the API gateway.
Combine into a candidate population of PI-bearing systems with the discovery source per row.
Freeze the population with a row count and timestamp before sampling.
testing.done: a frozen candidate population of PI-bearing systems exists with discovery sources independent of the register.

testing.step: Reconcile the candidate population to the register and prove completeness
actions: Match each candidate system to a register row and list every unmatched system holding California PI.
For each unmatched system, obtain the owner's written confirmation of what PI it holds and how long it has been live.
List register rows referring to decommissioned systems and confirm each has a retirement date.
Quantify unregistered stores and the estimated record volume behind them.
testing.done: unregistered PI stores are named and quantified, and stale register rows are reconciled to retirement dates.

testing.step: Draw the register and request samples with a recorded method
actions: Take 100% of register rows carrying sensitive PI and 100% flagged as sale or sharing.
Take 25 further register rows at random from the remainder with a recorded seed.
Take 100% of access requests marked BREACH or extended, plus 25 random closed requests from the quarter.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and selection date so both samples can be redrawn.
testing.done: both samples are drawn, stratified on sensitive and sale/share rows and on breached and extended requests, and are reproducible.

testing.step: Re-perform the field-level classification on sampled stores
actions: Run an independent column profile over each sampled store and compare the detected PI columns to the register's category list.
Query five columns per store directly and eyeball the values to confirm the classification is right, not just plausible.
Flag any store where sensitive PI is present but not flagged, since that changes the notice and the Limit-Use obligation.
Record undetected categories per store as completeness exceptions.
testing.done: each sampled store has an independent classification result and every undetected or misflagged category is recorded.

testing.step: Challenge the purpose and proportionality reasoning
actions: Read the stated collection purpose and business purpose for each sampled row against the notice at collection given to the consumer at that point.
Apply the 11 CCR 7002 reasonably-necessary-and-proportionate test yourself and record agreement or a specific objection.
Reject rows whose business purpose is a bare statutory quotation with no link to what the data is actually used for.
Refer any purpose not disclosed in the notice to the notice owner as a disclosure gap.
testing.done: each sampled purpose is independently tested for proportionality and any undisclosed purpose is referred as a disclosure gap.

testing.step: Trace the recipient map to real contracts and real outbound feeds
actions: For each sampled row, take the named recipients and locate the executed contract in the CLM repository.
Compare the register's sale/share/disclosure classification to the contract's data-use restrictions and to the outbound feed configuration.
Query the API gateway and file-transfer job logs for outbound destinations that carry PI but are absent from the recipient map.
List every undocumented outbound flow with its destination and volume.
testing.done: each sampled recipient traces to an executed contract and any undocumented outbound PI flow is named with its volume.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day maths on every sampled access request
actions: Recompute elapsed calendar days from the raw intake timestamp to the response delivery timestamp for each sampled request.
Compare to the elapsed count stored on the ledger row and investigate any difference greater than one day.
For extended requests, confirm the extension notice date falls inside the first 45 days and the extended target is no more than 45 further days.
Recompute the 10-business-day confirmation count alongside and flag any request missing a confirmation entirely.
testing.done: every sampled request has an independently recomputed elapsed-day count reconciled to the ledger, with extension validity confirmed.

testing.step: Re-perform a right-to-know disclosure from the register and compare
actions: Take five sampled requests and rebuild the disclosure yourself from the register rows and lineage nodes in scope on the receipt date.
Compare your category list, source list, purpose list and recipient list to the disclosure actually sent to the consumer.
Confirm each withheld element is on the 11 CCR 7024(d) list and was named as withheld rather than silently dropped.
Record every category present in your rebuild but absent from the sent response as an under-disclosure exception.
testing.done: five disclosures are independently rebuilt and every under-disclosed category or improperly withheld element is recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception typed as register completeness, classification, purpose, recipient mapping, timing breach or under-disclosure.
Quantify the exposure — records, consumers, days over deadline, undocumented feed volume — on the issue.
Assign a root cause and a named owner in the system or fulfilment function responsible, with a remediation date inside 30 days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row and block the register attestation for that row until closed.
testing.done: every exception is typed, quantified, owned, dated and blocks the affected register row's next attestation until closed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Council
actions: Compute the register completeness rate, the attestation rate and the 45-day on-time rate and compare each to the zero-breach threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and attests no sampled register row, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Data Governance Council and the DPO and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completeness, attestation and on-time rates, a conclusion, and the Council reporting date.
