checklist.step: Screen every new or renewing supplier for California PI exposure
actions: Add the mandatory intake question set to the sourcing request: does the supplier receive, access or generate California resident PI, which categories, and by what transfer mechanism.
Where the answer is yes, attach the data-flow description — direction, frequency, volume, identifiers — and route the request to Privacy and Third-Party Risk before any award.
Block purchase-order release in the procurement workflow until the privacy review is stamped complete.
Record the screening outcome and reviewer on the sourcing record so a later audit can see who cleared it.
checklist.done: no supplier receiving California PI passes to award without a completed screening record and a privacy review stamp.

checklist.step: Classify the recipient as service provider, contractor or third party
actions: Read the data-flow description and decide the role: service provider (processes for a business purpose under written contract), contractor (same, with the certification), or third party (everything else, including ad platforms taking data for cross-context behavioural advertising).
Test the service-provider claim against 11 CCR 7051 — no retention, use or disclosure outside the contract, no combining with other sources beyond the permitted cases.
Where the flow is for cross-context behavioural advertising, classify it as sharing and mark it for the opt-out fan-out list.
Write the classification, its reasoning and the citation onto the vendor record; do not let commercial preference decide the label.
checklist.done: each vendor carries a documented service provider, contractor or third-party classification with a cited reasoning line.

checklist.step: Attach the matching clause set to the contract
actions: Select the CCPA addendum variant that matches the classification and attach it to the agreement in the CLM template engine.

Confirm the mandatory clauses are present and unedited: specified limited purposes, prohibition on selling or sharing the PI, prohibition on retaining, using or disclosing outside the contract, prohibition on combining with other personal information, the compliance certification, the right to audit and remediate, and the obligation to notify if the vendor can no longer meet its obligations.
For contractors, confirm the express certification that the contractor understands and will comply with the restrictions.
Add the flow-down obligation to subcontractors and the deletion-on-instruction clause that the deletion process depends on.
checklist.done: the executed draft carries the correct addendum variant with every mandatory clause present and unedited.

checklist.step: Clear any redline against the clause set with Privacy Counsel
actions: Read every supplier redline against the statutory clause list and reject deletions of the sell/share prohibition, the combination prohibition or the audit right outright.
Where wording changes are acceptable, record why the amended text still satisfies 1798.100(d) and 11 CCR 7051.
Escalate any supplier refusing the certification to the General Counsel with a recommendation to reclassify as a third party or walk away.
Stamp the approved deviation on the contract record with the counsel name and date.
checklist.done: no clause deviation reaches signature without a counsel-stamped rationale, and refusals are escalated rather than absorbed.

checklist.step: Execute the agreement and record the evidence
actions: Send the agreement with the addendum for signature and capture the completion certificate showing both signatories and timestamps.
File the executed set in the CLM with the effective date, the classification tag, the sale/share tag and the renewal date.
Release the procurement gate only after the executed document is filed, never on a promise of signature.
Notify the requesting business owner in writing that data transfer may now begin, with the date.
checklist.done: an executed addendum with a signature certificate is filed and the data transfer authorisation date is recorded.

checklist.step: Turn the executed terms into technical restrictions on the actual feed
actions: Configure the outbound feed to carry only the fields named in the contract's permitted purpose, dropping everything else at the gateway.
Apply the destination allow-list so the feed cannot be repointed without a change record referencing the contract.
Enable per-consumer suppression on the feed so an opt-out flag can stop an individual's record without stopping the whole integration.
Record the field list, destination and suppression capability on the vendor record.
checklist.done: the live feed carries only contracted fields, sits on an allow-listed destination and supports per-consumer suppression.

checklist.step: Maintain the definitive list of sale and sharing destinations
actions: List every destination that receives California PI for advertising or monetisation: ad platform audience uploads, pixel and SDK integrations, lead-exchange partners and data co-ops.
Tie each destination to its vendor contract record and its sale-or-share classification.
Compare the list to the tag manager container and the audience sync configuration monthly so a destination cannot be added quietly.
Publish the list as the fan-out target set used by the opt-out process.
checklist.done: a monthly-reconciled destination list exists, each row tied to a contract record and a sale/share classification.

checklist.step: Capture opt-out requests from every channel including preference signals
actions: Accept opt-outs from the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link, the toll-free line, the privacy inbox and authorised agents.
Treat a Global Privacy Control browser signal as a valid opt-out under 11 CCR 7025 without asking the consumer to confirm and without requiring verification.
Stamp the receipt date and the channel on the opt-out record and start the 15-business-day clock immediately.
Link the opt-out record to the known consumer profile where the signal can be tied to an identified individual, and to the browser identifier where it cannot.
checklist.done: opt-outs from every channel, including GPC signals, create a dated record with the 15-business-day clock running.

checklist.step: Fan the opt-out out to every destination inside 15 business days
actions: Set the sale/share suppression flag on the consumer record and push it to each destination on the published list through its own suppression mechanism.
Record the destination-level effective date and the confirmation reference returned by each platform.
Chase any destination without a confirmation by business day 10 and escalate to the Privacy Officer at business day 13.
Stop new audience syncs containing the identifier until every destination confirms.
checklist.done: each destination has a recorded suppression effective date and confirmation inside 15 business days, or an escalation exists.

checklist.step: Notify third parties that received the PI in the preceding 90 days
actions: Query the transfer logs for third parties that received the consumer's PI in the 90 days before the opt-out request date.
Send each the templated opt-out notification instructing them to stop selling or sharing that consumer's PI, per 11 CCR 7026(f)(2).
Log the notification date, recipient contact and any acknowledgement returned on the opt-out record.
Escalate non-acknowledging third parties to Contracts as a contract-performance issue with the clause reference.
checklist.done: every third party that received the PI in the prior 90 days has a logged opt-out notification and an acknowledgement or an escalation.

checklist.step: Confirm the opt-out back to the consumer and hold the state
actions: Send the consumer written confirmation that selling and sharing has stopped, with the effective date.
Set the record so no re-opt-in prompt is shown for at least 12 months, as 1798.135(c) requires.
Add the identifier to the permanent sale/share suppression list so a later data import cannot clear the flag.
Attach the confirmation to the opt-out record before closing it.
checklist.done: the consumer holds a dated confirmation, the 12-month no-reprompt rule is set and the identifier sits on the permanent suppression list.

checklist.step: Sweep the active vendor base for clause and classification drift
actions: Each quarter export all active vendors tagged as receiving California PI and check each has an executed addendum on the current clause version.
Re-test the classification against how the data is actually used now, not how it was described at onboarding — a service provider that started building its own audiences is a third party.
Raise a contract change request for every vendor on a superseded clause version, with a 90-day close date.
Report the drift count and the reclassification count to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: every active PI-receiving vendor is confirmed on the current clause version or carries a dated change request.

checklist.step: Exercise the audit and deletion rights the clauses grant
actions: Run the annual vendor assurance cycle: request the CCPA compliance certification, the deletion capability description and any SOC 2 or ISO report covering the PI environment.
For the highest-risk vendors, exercise the contractual audit right with an on-site or evidence-based review of retention, use and onward disclosure.
Test the deletion-on-instruction clause by issuing a live deletion instruction and requiring written confirmation with a record count.
File the assurance pack against the vendor record and raise findings as third-party risk issues.
checklist.done: each high-risk vendor has a dated assurance pack including a tested deletion confirmation with a record count.

checklist.step: Log vendor and opt-out exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise an issue for every vendor found receiving California PI without executed terms, every missing mandatory clause, and every opt-out not effective at a destination inside 15 business days.
Record exposure: consumers affected, destinations still receiving, days over the 15-business-day limit and the volume transferred without terms.
Assign the owner to Procurement, Contracts or Marketing Operations depending on the failure point, with a remediation date.
Require the feed to be suspended where a vendor has no executed terms, rather than remediating while data keeps flowing.
checklist.done: every failure has an issue with quantified exposure, an owner, a remediation date and, for unterminated flows, a suspension.

checklist.step: Retain the contract and opt-out evidence for the full period
actions: Archive executed addenda with signature certificates, classification worksheets, destination suppression confirmations and 90-day notification acknowledgements.
Apply the retention label of 7 years past contract termination and index by vendor, destination and consumer reference.
Confirm an opt-out record can be retrieved end to end — request, destination confirmations, downstream notifications, consumer confirmation.
Restore three vendor packs and three opt-out packs at random each quarter to prove retrievability.
checklist.done: vendor and opt-out evidence is archived, indexed and proven retrievable end to end by a quarterly restoration test.

testing.step: Build the population of vendors actually receiving California PI
actions: Export from the CLM every active vendor tagged as receiving California PI, with classification, addendum reference and clause version.
Independently pull the outbound integration list from the API gateway, the file-transfer job list, the tag manager container and the accounts-payable vendor spend list.
Merge into one population showing every supplier with a live PI path and its discovery source.
Freeze the population with a row count and timestamp before sampling.
testing.done: a frozen vendor population exists built from integration and spend evidence, not from the contract register alone.

testing.step: Reconcile live data flows to executed contracts
actions: Match each live outbound PI flow to an executed addendum with an effective date earlier than the flow's first transfer date.
List flows with no addendum, with an addendum executed after the transfers began, or on a superseded clause version.
Quantify the record volume transferred outside executed terms from the integration logs.
Require Contracts to explain each unmatched flow in writing and attach the reply.
testing.done: every live PI flow ties to a pre-dated executed addendum or is listed with the volume transferred outside terms.

testing.step: Draw the vendor and opt-out samples with a recorded method
actions: Take 100% of vendors classified as third parties and 100% of advertising and lead-exchange destinations.
Take 25 further vendors at random from the service-provider and contractor population using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of opt-outs arriving by Global Privacy Control signal plus 30 random opt-outs from other channels in the quarter.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and selection date so both samples can be redrawn.
testing.done: both samples are stratified on third parties, ad destinations and GPC opt-outs, and are reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the clause-by-clause check on each sampled contract
actions: Open the executed addendum and tick each mandatory element: limited specified purposes, no selling or sharing, no retention or use outside the contract, no combining with other PI, the compliance certification, the audit and remediation right, and the notify-on-inability obligation.
Compare the executed text to the approved template and list every edit with its effect.
Confirm any deviation carries a dated counsel approval that pre-dates execution.
Record a missing mandatory clause as a fail, not a documentation observation.
testing.done: each sampled contract has a clause-by-clause result and every deviation traces to a pre-dated counsel approval.

testing.step: Challenge the service-provider classification against actual data use
actions: For each sampled service provider, read the actual field list transferred and the vendor's own product description of what it does with the data.
Test the 11 CCR 7051 conditions: does the vendor combine the PI with other sources, build its own audiences, or retain beyond the engagement.
Reclassify as a third party any vendor whose real behaviour is sale or sharing, regardless of the contract label.
Record the evidence behind each reclassification and refer it to Contracts and to the notice owner.
testing.done: each sampled classification is independently re-tested against real data use and every mislabelled vendor is reclassified with evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the 15-business-day opt-out clock
actions: For each sampled opt-out, recompute business days from the raw channel timestamp to the earliest and latest destination suppression effective dates, excluding weekends and California state holidays.
Compare the recomputed count to the value stored on the opt-out record and investigate any difference.
Fail any destination whose effective date exceeds 15 business days from receipt, even where other destinations were on time.
Record the worst-case destination per opt-out as the case-level result.
testing.done: every sampled opt-out has an independently recomputed worst-case destination day count against the 15-business-day limit.

testing.step: Prove the suppression actually reached each destination
actions: For each sampled opt-out, open each destination's audience or suppression view and confirm the identifier is present in the suppression set and absent from active audiences.
Re-check 30 days after the effective date to confirm no re-import reintroduced the identifier.
For GPC opt-outs tied only to a browser identifier, confirm the pixel and SDK stop firing sale/share events for that identifier in the network trace.
Record the destination, view, timestamp and result for each check.
testing.done: every sampled opt-out is confirmed suppressed at each destination at the effective date and again 30 days later.

testing.step: Trace the 90-day downstream notifications
actions: For each sampled opt-out, query the transfer logs for third parties that received the PI in the 90 days before the request date.
Match each to a logged opt-out notification with a send date and, where returned, an acknowledgement.
List recipients with no notification and quantify how recently they received the PI.
Confirm non-acknowledging third parties were escalated to Contracts with the clause reference.
testing.done: every third party that received the PI in the prior 90 days is matched to a logged notification or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception typed as missing terms, missing clause, misclassification, late opt-out, failed suppression or missing downstream notification.
Quantify exposure — consumers, destinations, records transferred, days over the 15-business-day limit — on the issue.
Assign a root cause and a named owner in Procurement, Contracts or Marketing Operations and set a remediation date.
Require immediate feed suspension for any vendor without executed terms and carry all open exceptions into the next run as retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is typed, quantified, owned and dated, with feeds suspended where terms are absent.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the executed-terms coverage rate, the clause-completeness rate and the 15-business-day on-time rate against the zero-failure thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who negotiated no sampled contract and ran no fan-out, sign the workpaper.
Report to the General Counsel, the Privacy Officer and the Vendor Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the coverage, clause and on-time rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Privacy Office owns the per-initiative risk assessment gate for high-risk processing, including the documented identity-verification method used before any consumer request is actioned; the Data Protection Officer approves the residual-risk decision

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Civ. Code 1798.130 request-handling requirements read with CPPA regulations 11 CCR 7020 (methods for submitting requests), 7021 (timing) and 7022 (responding to deletion), together with the verification rules at 11 CCR 7060-7063 and the risk-assessment obligations for significant-risk processing at 11 CCR 7150-7157

In-scope processes.value: Any initiative that introduces or materially changes high-risk processing of California PI — automated decision-making in underwriting or claims triage, profiling for behavioural advertising, sensitive-PI use, telematics or precise geolocation, biometric identity checks — plus the design and periodic re-assessment of the consumer identity-verification method itself

In-scope systems.value: Assessment records with the risk register linkage and the DPO decision; initiative intake arrives from the delivery backlog and models are referenced in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Privacy Risk Assessment Procedure — screening questionnaire at initiative intake, the significant-risk trigger list, the benefits-versus-risks-to-consumers analysis, safeguards, residual risk decision, and the verification-tier design standard (two data points, three plus a signed declaration for specific pieces)

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Data Protection Officer and endorsed by the Enterprise Risk Committee; re-approved annually and immediately on any CPPA risk-assessment or automated decision-making rulemaking taking effect

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Screening completed within 5 business days of initiative intake; the full assessment completed and approved before the initiative's design freeze and always before any California PI is processed in production; every approved assessment reviewed at least every 3 years or on material change; the verification method re-assessed annually

Deadline reminders configured.value: Delivery-tool gate that blocks the design-freeze transition without an approved assessment id, GRC tasks at T-30/T-10 to the design-freeze date, and a 3-year re-assessment task raised automatically on each approved assessment

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Screening questionnaire, the completed assessment with the benefits-and-risks analysis, safeguard list, DPO approval and any conditions, retained 7 years past decommissioning of the processing it covers

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: High-risk processing found live without an approved assessment, or a request actioned outside the documented verification tier, is logged with the initiative or case reference, the consumers affected and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The DPO signs every residual-risk acceptance, every condition attached to an approval and every remediation of processing that went live without an assessment

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All initiatives that reached design freeze or production in the period per the delivery backlog, plus all live models and processing activities carrying a significant-risk flag, plus every consumer request verified in the quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero high-risk processing activities live without an approved assessment dated before first production processing; zero requests actioned at a weaker verification tier than the request type requires; any single instance escalates to the DPO and the Enterprise Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per initiative, so it is tested at every design-freeze gate and swept quarterly across initiatives that went live in the quarter; verification-tier testing runs quarterly over that quarter's verified requests

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored, reviewed or approved any assessment in the sample, nor verified any sampled request

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly assessment-gate workpaper (initiative population, gate reconciliation, assessment re-performance, verification sample, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under CCPA / Risk Assessments / <year>-Q<n>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment register with initiative, processing description, risk conclusion, safeguards and approval date, plus the written verification procedure and verification outcome logs, in the abridged form a CPPA submission would take, producible within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Counsel owns any CPPA request for risk assessments and decides what is submitted versus withheld as privileged; the DPO certifies the completeness of the assessment register before release

checklist.step: Screen every initiative at intake for high-risk processing
actions: Attach the privacy screening questionnaire to the initiative epic as a mandatory field set at intake, covering PI categories, populations, new data sources, automated decisions and advertising use.
Ask the initiative sponsor directly whether the change touches sensitive PI, precise geolocation, biometrics, telematics or profiling, and record the answers verbatim.
Submit the completed screening to the Privacy Office within 5 business days of intake.
Link the screening record id to the epic so the delivery gate can read it later.
checklist.done: every initiative epic carries a completed screening questionnaire linked by id within 5 business days of intake.

checklist.step: Triage the screening against the significant-risk trigger list
actions: Apply the trigger list: selling or sharing PI, processing sensitive PI, automated decision-making with a significant effect on the consumer, profiling in a workplace or public place, and training an automated decision system on personal information.
Where any trigger fires, open a full assessment record and set the required-by date to the initiative's design-freeze date.
Where no trigger fires, record a documented no-assessment decision with the reason rather than closing silently.
Notify the initiative's Project Manager of the outcome and the assessment id the same day.
checklist.done: each screening ends in either an opened assessment tied to the design-freeze date or a written no-assessment decision with a reason.

checklist.step: Describe the processing precisely enough to assess it
actions: Write the processing description: purpose, PI and sensitive-PI categories, consumer populations, sources, volumes, retention, recipients and the operational context.
Name the technology involved — model, vendor tool, tracking pixel, device — and where in the customer journey it operates.
Pull the corresponding processing-register rows so the description agrees with the recorded purposes rather than restating the business case.
Have the initiative's product owner confirm the description matches what will actually be built.
checklist.done: a processing description exists that names purpose, categories, populations, volumes, recipients and the technology, confirmed by the product owner.

checklist.step: Weigh benefits against risks to consumers and write the conclusion
actions: Set out the benefits to Meridian, to the consumer and to the public, and the negative impacts on consumer privacy, as 11 CCR 7152 frames the analysis.
Name the specific harms in play — unfair denial of coverage or claim, discriminatory pricing effects, economic loss, loss of control over sensitive PI, physical or reputational harm.
State whether the risks to consumers outweigh the benefits, and say so plainly where they do rather than softening it.
Record the reasoning, not just a rating, so the conclusion can be re-read by a regulator.
checklist.done: a written benefits-versus-risks analysis names specific consumer harms and states a plain conclusion with its reasoning.

checklist.step: Assess automated decision-making and model behaviour where present
actions: Pull the model card, the training-data description and the feature list from the model governance repository for any model in scope.
Assess whether the decision has a significant effect on the consumer — coverage eligibility, pricing, claim acceptance, employment — which triggers pre-use notice and opt-out obligations.
Review disparate-impact testing results with the Model Risk Manager and record whether protected-class proxies are present in the feature set.
Define the human-review path and the explanation the consumer will receive on request, and record both.
checklist.done: each in-scope model has a recorded significance determination, disparate-impact result, human-review path and consumer explanation.

checklist.step: Design the safeguards that reduce the identified risks
actions: For each named harm, specify the safeguard: field minimisation, pseudonymisation, access restriction, retention shortening, opt-out availability, human review, or dropping the processing.
Name the owner and the delivery date for each safeguard and tie it to a delivery backlog item so it is built, not promised.
Confirm access controls with the IAM team so the new data set is not inherited by every existing role.
Record the residual risk after safeguards, separately from the inherent risk.
checklist.done: every named harm has an owned, dated safeguard tied to a backlog item, with inherent and residual risk recorded separately.

checklist.step: Write the identity-verification method into the assessment
actions: Document the verification tiers: two matching data points for a categories-only request, three plus a signed declaration under penalty of perjury for specific pieces of PI, and the authorised-agent route with written permission.
Name the data points that may be used for matching and forbid matching against data supplied inside the request itself.
State that no additional PI is collected for verification beyond what is necessary, and that verification data is deleted as soon as practicable after use.
Define what happens when verification fails: the denial wording, the invitation to re-submit, and the record kept.
checklist.done: the written verification procedure states the tiers, permitted matching data, the no-extra-collection rule and the failure path.

checklist.step: Assess the verification method itself as a processing activity
actions: Treat verification as its own high-risk processing where it collects identity documents or biometric checks, and run the benefits-and-risks analysis on it.
Balance the risk of unauthorised disclosure from weak verification against the risk of over-collection from heavy verification, and record where the line was set.
Set the retention for verification artefacts and the deletion job that enforces it.
Re-run this assessment annually or whenever a new verification vendor or method is introduced.
checklist.done: the verification method has its own risk analysis with a stated balance point, an artefact retention rule and an annual re-assessment date.

checklist.step: Instrument the verification decision so every outcome is logged
actions: Add mandatory fields to the case form: tier applied, data points matched, declaration received, verifier id and verification date.
Block case progression to fulfilment until the verification fields are populated, so a request cannot be answered unverified.
Log verification failures with the reason code and the follow-up sent to the consumer.
Expose the verification outcome fields to reporting so the tier mix can be monitored.
checklist.done: fulfilment is technically blocked until verification fields are complete, and every outcome including failures is logged with a reason.

checklist.step: Route the assessment through review and DPO approval
actions: Review the processing description, the benefits-and-risks analysis, the safeguards and the residual-risk statement in one package.
Approve, approve with conditions, or reject; where conditions are set, name each condition, its owner and its date.
Refuse approval where a stated harm has no safeguard, rather than accepting residual risk by default.
Stamp the approval with the DPO name and date and release the assessment id to the delivery gate.
checklist.done: the assessment carries a dated DPO decision with any conditions named, owned and dated, and a released assessment id.

checklist.step: Enforce the gate at design freeze and again before production
actions: Configure the design-freeze transition to require an approved assessment id on the initiative record.
Re-check at the production release gate that the built solution still matches the assessed processing description, and re-open the assessment where scope moved.
Hold the release where any approval condition is still open past its date, and record the hold decision.
Report gate holds and overrides weekly to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: no initiative passes design freeze or production release without an approved, scope-matched assessment and closed conditions.

checklist.step: Track approval conditions and safeguards to completion
actions: Open a tracked action per approval condition and per safeguard with the owner and due date from the assessment.
Verify completion with evidence — a configuration screenshot, an access-control export, a retention job schedule — not with an owner's assertion.
Escalate any condition overdue by 30 days to the DPO with a recommendation to suspend the processing.
Close the assessment only when every condition has evidenced completion.
checklist.done: every condition and safeguard is evidenced complete or escalated at 30 days overdue, and assessments close only on evidence.

checklist.step: Re-assess on material change and on the three-year cycle
actions: Raise a re-assessment when the processing adds a PI category, a new population, a new recipient, a new model version or a new purpose.
Run the calendar re-assessment at least every three years for every live approved assessment, refreshing volumes and harms rather than re-signing the old text.
Retire assessments for decommissioned processing with a decommission date and confirmation the data was deleted or de-identified.
Report the re-assessment backlog monthly to the DPO.
checklist.done: every live assessment is inside its three-year cycle or has a raised re-assessment, and retired ones carry a decommission date.

checklist.step: Log assessment and verification exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every high-risk processing activity found live without an approved assessment, and for every request actioned below the required verification tier.
Record the exposure: consumers processed without assessment, records disclosed on weak verification, and the days the gap ran.
Assign a root cause — screening skipped at intake, scope grew after approval, gate overridden, verification field bypassed — and an owner.
Require the processing to be paused where consumer harm is credible, rather than remediating in flight.
checklist.done: every gate and verification failure has an issue with quantified exposure, a root cause, an owner and a pause decision where harm is credible.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment record in the form a regulator may demand
actions: File the screening, the full assessment, the safeguard evidence, the DPO approval and the condition closures as one indexed pack per initiative.
Maintain the abridged assessment register — initiative, processing purpose, categories, risk conclusion, approval date — in the form a CPPA submission takes.
Apply the retention label of 7 years past decommissioning of the processing.
Restore three assessment packs at random each quarter and confirm every artefact opens and the approval signature is intact.
checklist.done: each initiative has one indexed assessment pack under a 7-year label, with a maintained abridged register and quarterly restoration proof.

testing.step: Build the population of initiatives and live high-risk processing
actions: Export every initiative that passed design freeze or went to production in the period, with dates and sponsor.
Independently pull the model inventory from the model governance repository, the processing register rows flagged sensitive or sale/share, and the tag manager list of new advertising trackers.
Merge into one population of processing activities that should have been assessed, showing the discovery source per row.
Freeze the population with a row count and timestamp before sampling.
testing.done: a frozen population of assessable processing activities exists, built from delivery, model and register sources independently.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to screenings and approved assessments
actions: Match each population row to a screening record and, where a trigger fired, to an approved assessment.
Check the assessment approval date pre-dates the first production processing date taken from the release log.
List rows with no screening, with a screening but no assessment despite a trigger, or with an assessment approved after go-live.
Require the Privacy Office to explain each unmatched row in writing and attach the reply.
testing.done: every processing activity ties to a screening and, where triggered, to an assessment approved before go-live, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the assessment and verification samples with a recorded method
actions: Take 100% of assessments covering automated decision-making with a significant effect and 100% covering sensitive PI.
Take 15 further approved assessments at random from the remainder using a recorded seed.
Take 40 verified consumer requests from the quarter, stratified to include every specific-pieces request and every authorised-agent request.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and selection date so both samples can be redrawn.
testing.done: both samples are stratified on automated decisions, sensitive PI, specific-pieces and agent requests, and are reproducible.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk analysis on each sampled assessment
actions: Read the processing description and form your own view of the consumer harms before reading the recorded analysis.
Compare your harm list to the assessment's and record any harm the assessment omitted, particularly discriminatory pricing and unfair denial effects.
Test whether the stated conclusion actually follows from the analysis or was written to reach a permissive answer.
Confirm the assessment names safeguards for every harm it identified and flag any harm left unsafeguarded.
testing.done: each sampled assessment has an independent harm list, a follows-from-the-analysis verdict and any unsafeguarded harm named.

testing.step: Test that assessed scope matches what was actually built
actions: Compare the assessed PI categories, populations and recipients to the live configuration: the field list in the data store, the audience destinations and the model feature list.
Flag every category, population, feature or recipient present in production but absent from the assessment as scope drift.
Check whether scope drift triggered a re-assessment, and when.
Quantify the consumers processed under the drifted scope from the production volumes.
testing.done: each sampled assessment is compared field by field to production and all scope drift is quantified by consumers affected.

testing.step: Verify safeguards and approval conditions were actually implemented
actions: For each safeguard, pull the implementing evidence — access group membership export, retention job schedule, masking configuration, opt-out toggle — and test it directly.
Confirm access to the new data set is limited to the roles named in the assessment and list any role that inherited access outside it.
Confirm every approval condition is closed with evidence and note conditions closed on assertion alone.
Record safeguards that exist on paper but not in the configuration as control failures.
testing.done: every sampled safeguard and condition is directly tested in the live configuration and paper-only controls are recorded as failures.

testing.step: Re-perform the identity verification on sampled requests
actions: For each sampled request, read the request type and decide the required tier yourself before opening the verification record.
Confirm the recorded data points were matched against pre-existing records and that specific-pieces requests carry three points plus the signed declaration.
Confirm no PI was collected for verification beyond the documented list, and that verification artefacts were deleted per the stated retention.
Record any request fulfilled below the required tier as an over-disclosure exception with the records disclosed.
testing.done: each sampled request has an independent tier verdict and any over-disclosure is quantified by records released.

testing.step: Test the gate controls by attempting to bypass them
actions: In a test initiative, attempt the design-freeze transition without an assessment id and confirm the transition is refused.
In a test case, attempt to move to fulfilment with the verification fields blank and confirm progression is blocked.
Pull the override log for both gates and list every production override with its approver and reason.
Confirm each override carries a DPO or Privacy Officer approval rather than a delivery-side approval.
testing.done: both gates are proven to block by direct test, and every production override is listed with an approver and a reason.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception typed as missing screening, missing assessment, late approval, scope drift, unimplemented safeguard, gate override or verification shortfall.
Quantify exposure — consumers processed unassessed, records disclosed on weak verification, days the gap ran.
Assign a root cause and a named owner in the delivery or privacy function responsible, with a remediation date.
Recommend suspension of any processing running unassessed where the harm analysis suggests credible consumer impact.
testing.done: every exception is typed, quantified, owned and dated, with suspension recommended where consumer harm is credible.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the assessment coverage rate, the pre-go-live approval rate, the safeguard implementation rate and the verification-tier compliance rate.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and approved no sampled assessment, sign the workpaper.
Report to the DPO and the Enterprise Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the four rates, a conclusion and the Enterprise Risk Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: The CISO owns incident detection, containment and the breach notification decision jointly with the Privacy Officer; Privacy Ops owns the downstream deletion directives issued to service providers and contractors after a consumer deletion

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Civ. Code 1798.105 and CPPA regulation 11 CCR 7022(b)(3)-(4) for the obligation to instruct service providers, contractors and third parties to delete, read with Civ. Code 1798.82 (notification in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, content requirements and the sample-notice filing with the California Attorney General above 500 residents) and 1798.150 for the unencrypted-and-unredacted exposure limb

In-scope processes.value: Security incident triage through to consumer and regulator notification for any incident touching California resident PI, plus the deletion-directive fan-out to every service provider, contractor and third party that received PI for a consumer whose deletion request was executed

In-scope systems.value: Detection and case management for incidents, with the security ticketing system holding the incident record; deletion directives are issued and tracked from the DSAR case with confirmations filed against the vendor record

Compliance procedure documented.value: Privacy Incident and Downstream Deletion Procedure — severity model, the 'was PI unencrypted and unredacted' determination, the notification decision matrix by jurisdiction, notice content template, AG sample-notice filing, and the deletion-directive template with the confirmation chase cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the CISO and the General Counsel, endorsed at the Enterprise Risk Committee; tabletop-tested at least annually and re-approved after every tabletop or live incident review

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Consumer notice in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, with an internal target of 30 calendar days from confirmation of the breach; a sample copy of the notice filed with the California Attorney General when more than 500 California residents are notified, filed on or before the consumer send date; deletion directives issued to service providers and contractors within 5 business days of executing the deletion, with confirmations back inside 30 calendar days

Deadline reminders configured.value: SOAR playbook timers at hour 24 (scoping due), day 5 (notification decision due), day 20 (notice drafted and approved) and day 28 (send or explain), plus deletion-directive chasers at day 10, day 20 and day 28 escalating to the Vendor Manager and the Privacy Officer

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Incident record with the detection and confirmation timestamps, the scoping analysis and affected-resident count, the notification decision memo, the sent notices with the mailing or email evidence, the AG submission receipt, and the deletion directives with per-vendor confirmations, retained 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A notification sent beyond the internal 30-day target without a documented law-enforcement delay, an AG sample notice not filed above the 500-resident threshold, or a deletion directive not issued or not confirmed, is logged with the incident or case reference, the residents affected and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs the notification decision including every decision not to notify, the notice text, the AG filing, and any remediation of a late notice or an unconfirmed deletion directive

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All security and privacy incidents raised in the period with any California PI exposure indicator, plus all executed consumer deletion requests in the period with their downstream directive records

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly incident and deletion-directive workpaper (incident population, day-count recomputation, notice content check, directive tracing, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under CCPA / Incident and Deletion / <year>-<month>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Incident chronology with detection, confirmation, scoping and notification timestamps, the notice as sent, the California AG submission receipt, and the deletion-directive register with vendor confirmations, producible to the AG or the CPPA within 5 business days

checklist.step: Detect and raise the incident with a hard timestamp
actions: Triage the alert against the detection rules for PI exfiltration, mass export, unauthorised database access and misdirected bulk mail.
Raise the incident ticket immediately with the detection timestamp taken from the source log, not from the analyst's shift time.
Set the initial severity from the data-classification of the affected store and page the Incident Response Lead for anything touching Restricted data.
Attach the triggering log excerpt and the affected host or account list to the ticket.
checklist.done: an incident ticket exists with a source-log detection timestamp, initial severity and the triggering evidence attached.

checklist.step: Contain the incident and preserve the evidence
actions: Isolate affected endpoints, revoke compromised sessions and credentials with the IAM team, and block the exfiltration path at the gateway.
Take forensic images and preserve logs before any rebuild, and record the chain of custody with times and handlers.
Open the incident bridge and record decisions with timestamps so the chronology writes itself.
Notify the CISO and the Privacy Officer within one hour of confirming Restricted data involvement.
checklist.done: the incident is contained, evidence is preserved under a recorded chain of custody, and the CISO and Privacy Officer were notified within one hour.

checklist.step: Scope exactly which California residents and which data elements were exposed
actions: Reconstruct the accessed or exfiltrated record set from the query logs, file access logs and egress captures rather than estimating from table size.
Join the record set to the customer master to produce a deduplicated list of affected individuals with state of residence.

List the data elements per individual, flagging Social Security number, driver's licence or California ID number, financial account number, medical information and health insurance information, since those drive both notification and the credit-monitoring offer.
State for each element whether it was encrypted and whether the key was also compromised, because that determines whether 1798.82 and 1798.150 bite.
Deliver the affected-resident count and the element matrix to Privacy Counsel with the reconstruction method documented.
checklist.done: a deduplicated affected-resident list exists with per-element exposure and an encryption determination, with the method documented.

checklist.step: Make and record the notification decision
actions: Apply the Civ. Code 1798.82 test: was unencrypted and unredacted personal information of a California resident acquired, or reasonably believed acquired, by an unauthorised person.
Where the encryption safe harbour is claimed, record the algorithm, key management and the evidence the key was not compromised.
Decide notification per jurisdiction where residents span states, and record the decision, the reasoning and the decision date in a signed memo.
Where law enforcement requests a delay, obtain it in writing with the requesting agency, officer and expected duration, and diarise the re-test date.
checklist.done: a signed, dated decision memo states notify or not-notify per jurisdiction with the statutory test applied and any law-enforcement delay documented.

checklist.step: Draft the consumer notice to the statutory content list
actions: Build the notice on the required headings — What Happened, What Information Was Involved, What We Are Doing, What You Can Do, For More Information — in plain language at 10-point type or larger.

Include the name and contact details of the reporting entity, the types of PI involved, the date or date range of the breach, and the toll-free numbers and addresses of the three major credit reporting agencies.

Where Social Security, driver's licence or California ID numbers were involved, include the offer of identity theft prevention and mitigation services at no cost for at least 12 months with instructions to take it up.
Have Privacy Counsel approve the text and the delivery method before anything is printed or queued.
checklist.done: an approved notice exists carrying every statutory element, with the 12-month monitoring offer where identifier types require it.

checklist.step: Deliver the notice and prove delivery
actions: Send by written notice to the last known postal address, or by electronic notice only where the consumer consented to electronic communication under the federal E-SIGN standard.

Where the cost would exceed 250,000 dollars, the affected class exceeds 500,000 people, or contact details are insufficient, use substitute notice — email where available, a conspicuous website posting for at least 30 days, and notification to major statewide media — and record which limb was relied on.
Reconcile the send file back to the affected-resident list and chase every undeliverable through address-append before writing it off.
Stand up the dedicated response line and the FAQ before the notices land, and brief the contact centre with the approved holding statement.
checklist.done: the send file reconciles to the affected-resident list, undeliverables are chased, and the response line is live before delivery.

checklist.step: File the sample notice with the California Attorney General above 500 residents
actions: Where more than 500 California residents are notified in a single breach, open the Attorney General's data breach reporting form at oag.ca.gov and submit a sample copy of the notice with the identifying information redacted.
Complete the submission fields: organisation name and type, breach date range, discovery date, notification date, number of Californians notified and data types involved.
Capture the submission confirmation and the public listing reference and file both against the incident record.
Submit on or before the date the consumer notices go out, never after.
checklist.done: the AG sample-notice submission is completed with a captured confirmation reference, dated on or before the consumer send date.

checklist.step: Notify the affected business partners and the insurance regulator where required
actions: Where the compromised data belongs to a group client, broker or reinsurer, issue the contractual breach notice inside the period the contract specifies and log the send.
Assess whether the California Department of Insurance or any other domiciliary regulator requires notification under the insurer's licensing conditions and record the assessment either way.
Where Meridian was acting as a service provider to another business, notify that business immediately so it can run its own notification duty.
Track every partner notification with recipient, date, method and acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every contractual and regulatory partner notification is assessed, sent where required, and logged with an acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Issue deletion directives to service providers and contractors after a consumer deletion
actions: On executing a consumer deletion, pull from the recipient map every service provider and contractor that received that consumer's PI.
Send each the templated deletion directive within 5 business days, naming the consumer identifiers, the deletion date and the required confirmation, per 11 CCR 7022(b)(3).

Where the PI was sold or shared, additionally notify every third party that received it, unless a statutory impossibility or disproportionate-effort exception applies — and record the exception with its reasoning.
Log each directive on the DSAR case with recipient, send date, method and the response due date.
checklist.done: every recipient of the consumer's PI has a dated deletion directive on the case within 5 business days, with any exception reasoned.

checklist.step: Chase and record the downstream deletion confirmations
actions: Track each outstanding directive and chase at day 10 and day 20 against a 30-calendar-day confirmation target.
Require the confirmation to state the systems purged, the record count and the deletion or de-identification method, not a bare acknowledgement.
Escalate non-responders to the contract owner as a breach of the deletion-on-instruction clause and record the escalation.
File each confirmation against both the DSAR case and the vendor record.
checklist.done: each directive has a substantive confirmation with systems, counts and method, or a logged escalation under the contract clause.

checklist.step: Tell the consumer what happened to their downstream data
actions: In the deletion response, state that service providers and contractors were instructed to delete and name the categories of recipient involved.
Where an exception prevented a directive or a recipient could not delete, tell the consumer which category and why, citing the exception relied on.
Offer the consumer the route to challenge the outcome and record any challenge received.
Attach the response to the case with the delivery evidence.
checklist.done: the consumer response states the downstream directive outcome, names any exception relied on and gives a challenge route.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and fix the cause
actions: Hold the review within 15 business days of closure with the incident chronology, the notification timeline and the scoping method on the table.
Identify the control that failed — detection gap, excessive access, unencrypted store, missing egress control — and raise a remediation action with an owner and a date.
Assess whether the same control gap exists in adjacent systems and extend the remediation there.
Report the incident, the notification timeline and the remediation plan to the Enterprise Risk Committee.
checklist.done: a post-incident review is held within 15 business days with owned, dated remediation actions extended to adjacent systems.

checklist.step: Exercise the plan on a tabletop at least annually
actions: Run a scenario involving unencrypted California PI at a service provider, forcing both the notification decision and the downstream directive path.
Time-stamp each decision in the exercise and compare to the 30-day notice target and the 5-business-day directive target.
Record every plan defect surfaced — an unreachable contact, an unclear decision owner, a missing template — as an action with an owner.
Update the procedure and re-approve it with the CISO and General Counsel after the exercise.
checklist.done: an annual tabletop is run against timed targets with every plan defect actioned and the procedure re-approved.

checklist.step: Log incident and directive exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every notice sent beyond the 30-day target without a documented delay, every missing AG filing above 500 residents, and every deletion directive not issued or not confirmed.
Record the exposure — residents affected, days late, recipients unconfirmed — and the root cause.
Assign the owner to the function that caused the delay: detection, scoping, legal decision, print and mail, or vendor management.
Carry unresolved items into the next monthly test as mandatory retest rows.
checklist.done: every timing and directive failure has an issue with exposure, root cause, an owner and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Retain the incident and directive record for the full period
actions: Archive the incident chronology, scoping analysis, decision memo, approved notice, send file and delivery evidence, AG submission receipt and post-incident review as one indexed pack.
Archive the deletion directives with their confirmations against both the DSAR case and the vendor record.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by incident reference, resident count and consumer reference.
Restore one incident pack and three directive sets each quarter to prove retrievability.
checklist.done: incident and directive evidence is archived complete, indexed and proven retrievable by a quarterly restoration test.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents and executed deletions
actions: Export every security and privacy incident raised in the period with severity, affected data classification and closure status.
Independently pull SIEM alerts tagged for data exfiltration or mass export, the DLP alert log and the misdirected-mail complaint log so incidents never ticketed surface.
Export every executed consumer deletion in the period from the DSAR case tool with its recipient map.
Freeze both populations with row counts and timestamps before sampling.
testing.done: frozen incident and deletion populations exist, with incidents cross-built from SIEM, DLP and complaint sources.

testing.step: Reconcile alerts to incident tickets and deletions to directive records
actions: Match each exfiltration, DLP and misdirected-mail alert to an incident ticket and list unticketed alerts as detection-control failures.
Match each executed deletion to a directive record for every recipient on its recipient map.
List deletions with no directive, or with directives to fewer recipients than the map holds.
Require Security Operations and Privacy Ops to explain each unmatched row in writing and attach the replies.
testing.done: every alert ties to a ticket and every deletion ties to a complete directive set, or the gap is listed with a written explanation.

testing.step: Draw the samples with a documented, reproducible method
actions: Take 100% of incidents classified as notifiable and 100% of incidents involving Social Security, driver's licence or financial account numbers.
Take 20 further incidents at random from the remainder using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of deletions where PI had been sold or shared, plus 25 random executed deletions.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and selection date so both samples can be redrawn.
testing.done: both samples are stratified on notifiable incidents, high-risk identifiers and sold-or-shared deletions, and are reproducible.

testing.step: Recompute the notification clock from the raw timestamps
actions: For each sampled incident recompute calendar days from the source-log detection timestamp to the confirmation timestamp, and from confirmation to the consumer notice send date.
Compare to the 30-day internal target and to the 'most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay' standard, and challenge any long gap between containment and decision.
Where a law-enforcement delay is claimed, confirm the written request names the agency and officer and that notice followed promptly once the hold lifted.
Recompute the deletion-directive clock as business days from deletion execution to directive send against the 5-business-day target.
testing.done: every sampled incident and deletion has independently recomputed day counts against the 30-day and 5-business-day targets.

testing.step: Re-perform the notifiability determination
actions: Read the scoping analysis and apply the 1798.82 test yourself before reading the decision memo.
Where an encryption safe harbour was claimed, test the algorithm, key custody and the evidence the key was uncompromised, and reject bare assertions of encryption at rest.
Where a not-notifiable decision was reached, challenge whether 'reasonably believed acquired' was applied honestly against the log evidence.
Record agreement or disagreement per incident with the reasoning.
testing.done: each sampled decision is independently re-determined and every encryption safe-harbour claim is tested against key evidence.

testing.step: Re-perform the affected-resident scoping on a sub-sample
actions: For three sampled incidents, rebuild the affected record set from the raw access and egress logs without reference to the responder's output.
Deduplicate to individuals and compare your California resident count to the count used for the notification and the AG threshold.
Compare the per-element exposure matrix and flag any element the original scoping missed, particularly identifiers that trigger the credit-monitoring offer.
Quantify any undercount as residents who should have been notified but were not.
testing.done: three incidents have independently rebuilt resident counts and element matrices, with any undercount quantified in residents.

testing.step: Check the notice content and the AG filing
actions: Score each sampled notice against the statutory elements: entity name and contact, types of PI, breach date or range, description of the incident, credit agency contacts, and the 12-month identity-theft services offer where required.
Confirm the required headings are present and the type size and plain-language standard are met on the printed sample.
For every incident above 500 California residents, locate the AG submission confirmation and confirm its date is on or before the consumer send date.
Confirm the sample notice filed matches the notice actually sent, not an earlier draft.
testing.done: each sampled notice is scored element by element and every above-threshold incident shows a matching, timely AG filing.

testing.step: Trace deletion directives to substantive vendor confirmations
actions: For each sampled deletion, list the recipients from the recipient map and match each to a sent directive with a date.
Open each confirmation and check it names the systems purged, the record count and the method, rejecting bare acknowledgements.
For sold or shared PI, confirm third parties were notified or that a documented impossibility or disproportionate-effort exception was recorded with reasoning.
Confirm non-responding vendors were escalated against the contractual deletion clause.
testing.done: every recipient traces to a dated directive and a substantive confirmation, an exception with reasoning, or a logged contract escalation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception typed as detection gap, scoping undercount, late notice, deficient notice content, missing AG filing, missing directive or unconfirmed deletion.
Quantify exposure — residents affected or unnotified, days late, recipients unconfirmed.
Assign a root cause and a named owner in Security Operations, Privacy Ops, Legal or Vendor Management, with a remediation date.
Refer any undercount that left residents unnotified to Privacy Counsel for a supplemental notification decision within 5 business days.
testing.done: every exception is typed, quantified, owned and dated, with undercounts referred for a supplemental notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time notification rate, the notice content completeness rate, the AG filing rate and the directive issue-and-confirm rate.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the incident response chain, sign the workpaper.
Report to the CISO, the General Counsel and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the four rates, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.
